items.headline: James Harden turns back the clock — 51 points in Cleveland
items.body: The Beard dropped a vintage 51 points with seven threes to power the Cavaliers past the Pacers 128-119 on Friday night. Not bad for a guy in his mid-thirties who's supposedly past his prime — he just outscored whole teams by himself.
items.say: James Harden went for 51 last night — seven threes, the whole show. The guy's still cooking in his thirties. You catching any NBA this season?

items.headline: Jokić and Şengün trade monster lines in a Nuggets-Rockets shootout
items.body: Two of the best big men on the planet put on a passing clinic: Alperen Şengün stuffed the sheet with a 28-11-10 triple-double, but Nikola Jokić answered with 26 points and 11 assists to lead Denver to a 133-124 win. Point-centers doing point-guard things.
items.say: Jokić and Şengün both went off last night — a triple-double for one, 26 and 11 for the other. Watching those two big guys pass is unreal. You a Jokić fan?

items.headline: Man City stumble again — Fulham grab a point and snap a 14-year drought
items.body: Fulham hadn't beaten or drawn City in the league in 14 years — until today. Rodrigo Muniz struck early and Fulham held on for a 1-1 draw, Elliot Anderson leveling it in the second half. It stretches champions-chasing City's winless league run to four games.
items.say: Fulham just held Man City to a draw — first time they've taken points off them in like 14 years. City are suddenly wobbling a bit. You follow the Premier League at all?

links.text: City's 14-year run vs Fulham ends in a draw (AP)

items.headline: The odds are ever in its favor — 'Sunrise on the Reaping' opens huge
items.body: The new Hunger Games prequel landed in theaters and the numbers are massive: $21.25 million in Thursday previews — the franchise's second-best ever — with the weekend tracking north of $110 million. It's young Haymitch's brutal story, and it's the movie everyone's seeing this weekend.
items.say: The new Hunger Games — young Haymitch's story — opened huge, one of the biggest debuts the series has ever had. Those movies still pull a crowd. You into the Hunger Games, or know someone counting down?

links.text: Sunrise on the Reaping — Official Trailer (The Hunger Games)

items.headline: Amy Poehler and Hugh Laurie go digging — 'Dig' hits Peacock Monday
items.body: From Mike Schur (Parks and Rec, The Good Place), 'Dig' drops all 10 episodes Monday on Peacock. Amy Poehler leads a crew of archaeologists in Greece who unearth a possibly history-changing artifact — and tumble into an international caper. Hugh Laurie co-stars.
items.say: There's a new Amy Poehler comedy on Peacock Monday — same guy who made Parks and Rec, with Hugh Laurie in it too. Looks like an easy fun one. You a Parks and Rec person?

items.headline: Back to Maple Brook — 'The Hunting Wives' returns next week
items.body: Netflix's soapy Texas thriller — all big hair, bigger secrets and Malin Åkerman and Brittany Snow at the center of it — comes back for Season 2 on November 26. It was a word-of-mouth smash the first time around, so a bingeable holiday-week guilty pleasure is loading.
items.say: The Hunting Wives is back on Netflix next week — that trashy-in-the-best-way Texas thriller everyone got hooked on. Perfect holiday-week binge. You watch the first season?

links.text: The Hunting Wives: Season 2 — Official Trailer (Netflix)

items.headline: 100 years of giant balloons — the Macy's Parade turns a century old
items.body: The Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade hits its 100th edition Thursday (8:30 a.m. ET on NBC and Peacock) with a record haul of inflatables. New balloons include Bluey and Hello Kitty, there's a Dolly Parton tribute, and Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots are among the acts.
items.say: The Macy's parade is turning 100 this year — new Bluey and Hello Kitty balloons, a Dolly Parton tribute, the works. It's such a cozy Thanksgiving-morning thing. You usually have it on?

links.text: Meet the new balloons for the 100th parade (NBC New York)

items.headline: GTA VI's soundtrack is an all-star album of its own
items.body: Alongside the record-smashing game, Rockstar dropped 'Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album' — 34 brand-new, original tracks made for the game's neon Vice City world. The guest list is absurd: Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Travis Scott, SZA, Tame Impala and a dozen more.
items.say: The new GTA has a whole original album to go with it — Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Travis Scott, all making songs just for the game. Kind of a flex. You messing with GTA 6, or just the soundtrack?
